LG Electronics' Preliminary Earnings Miss Street Views
By Kwanwoo Jun

LG Electronics forecast softer-than-expected third-quarter operating profit, though steady earnings growth keeps the South Korean consumer-electronics giant on course for an earnings recovery this year.

The preliminary earnings come as LG continues to expand into fast-growing businesses in the AI era, such as data-center cooling systems and robotics, while maintaining growth in its home-appliance and other core businesses despite challenges.

Operating profit likely reached 781.80 billion won, equivalent to $584.4 million, for the three months ended September, the company said Wednesday. That would be a 13.5% increase from 688.90 billion won in the year-ago period.
Analysts were looking for a bigger jump to 1.028 trillion won for the quarter, according to a FactSet-compiled consensus estimate.
Revenue is expected to have risen 8.9% to 23.827 trillion won, the company said, slightly below market expectations.
The company gave no further earnings details. It is slated to release full quarterly results later this month.

Shares fell nearly 7% in early trading after the preliminary results, paring strong year-to-date gains. LG Electronics' stock has more than doubled this year as the company expands its push into AI and new businesses.
Write to Kwanwoo Jun at kwanwoo.jun@wsj.com
